The stub is what makes this bite: STUB_CHECK_RUNS emits the second and later lines ONLY when the call carried the flag, so a read that stopped asking for pages stops getting them, which is the difference between a stub that proves the flag and one that proves only the join. The test it catches puts the failing run of the required check on page 2 and nothing about it on page 1: with the flag the mutant merges, so the refusal assertion fails. The single-page fixtures are invisible to it, because one page is all they ever had
